source_selection.exact_source_expression: When God says 'I AM WHO I AM,' He is not giving a label like other names. He is saying He cannot be defined by anything deeper or larger—He is the root, not a thing among things.
source_selection.reason: The claim has a clear logical structure: a self-naming entity that is not definable by anything deeper or larger, i.e., not a member of a larger category and not explained by a more fundamental entity. This can be modeled as a partial order of metaphysical dependence with a maximal element.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A root is an entity r such that there is no entity x with x < r in the dependence order, and r is not a member of any category C that is more fundamental than r.

symbol_table.reader_meaning: Any being or thing that can stand in dependence relations.
x depends on y if y is deeper, larger, or more fundamental than x.
An entity that is not dependent on anything deeper and is not a member of a more fundamental category.

explicit_premises: DependsOn is a strict partial order (irreflexive, transitive, asymmetric).
There exists at least one Entity.
assumptions_and_dependencies.theological_starting_premises: The biblical claim that God is the root and not a thing among things.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one entity satisfying Root, or the definition is vacuously true but not instantiated.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus was not searched; no compilation attempted.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal definition of a root entity in a dependence order.

result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The formalization captures the negative claim (not defined by anything deeper or larger) but does not capture the positive claim of self-existence or the personal nature of God.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Connects to classical theism's concept of God as ultimate ground of being.

source_selection.reason: The claim asserts a compatibility relation between two distinct epistemic sources: discovery (reason from world) and disclosure (revelation). This can be modeled as two sets of propositions that are consistent.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: If Discovery and Disclosure are sets of propositions, and both are true, then their union is consistent.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: Jesus doesn't just talk about God—He says things like 'I am the bread of life' and 'I am the truth,' using the same 'I am' language God used for Himself. That's identity language, not just religious advice.
source_selection.reason: The claim is about identity statements: Jesus uses 'I am' predicates that ascribe to Himself properties that are divine or ultimate. This can be modeled as a set of identity claims and a relation of 'divine predicate'.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A divine identity claim is a statement of the form 'Jesus is P' where P is a predicate that is also used of God in the Hebrew Bible or is a role that only God can fulfill.
